title: Reading a Profile's Return History over the Rolling Year — Northbeam Returns and Restocking
content:
Return behaviour on Northbeam Returns and Restocking is read across the whole profile rather than authorisation by authorisation: the count of authorisations raised in the rolling year, read from the count of authorisations raised on the profile in the rolling twelve calendar months ending on the handling date whose status is not withdrawn or denied, and the refund value settled in the rolling year, read from the sum of refund money paid out to the customer on every authorisation of the profile over the same rolling twelve calendar months, are both compared with the figures of the schedule the new line falls under. Where either figure is at or above its limit the return is still taken but is marked for review, the refund is settled only after the review closes, and store credit is used in place of a card refund. Authorisations that were withdrawn or refused do not count toward the count, because nothing came back; refunds later reversed do still count toward the value. A business contract profile is read against its own far larger figures, and the buyers named on it are counted together rather than one by one. Nothing in this rule refuses a return for a defective item, however often the profile has returned things.

## The two figures side by side

| | What is counted | Window | Compared with |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| The count | authorisations raised on the profile whose status is not withdrawn or denied | the rolling twelve calendar months ending on the handling date | the returns per rolling year figure of the schedule the new line falls under |
| The value | refund money paid out to the customer on every authorisation of the profile | the rolling twelve calendar months ending on the handling date | the review value of that same schedule |

## Points of judgement

**At or above, not above.** Either figure standing at its limit is enough to mark the profile for review; the comparison includes the limit itself.

**What review changes and what it does not.** Review changes when the refund is settled — only after the review closes — and the way it is paid, store credit standing in place of a card refund. The return itself is still taken.

**Two kinds of authorisation that do not count.** A withdrawn authorisation and a refused one both fall out of the count, on the ground that nothing came back. A refund that was later reversed is the other way about: it still counts toward the value.

**A business contract profile.** It is read against its own far larger figures, and every buyer named on it is counted together as one profile rather than buyer by buyer.

**A defective item.** Nothing in this rule refuses a return for a defective item, however often the profile has returned things.
